_note: tools/site.py builds the static page from this file, site/lang/*.json and site/index.html. Videos are copied from a media folder given at build time; each file's sha256 must equal its row in docs/MEASURED.md or the build stops. `vertical` is the first player on a phone, `film` on a wide screen; `short` is offered as a download link only. Only narrated versions belong here: a version ending in -tanpa-suara stops the build.

check._note: deploy/check_page.py: share of the 9:16 player's height a phone must show without scrolling

link_marks._note: tools/site.py: copy text between [[name]] and [[/name]] becomes a link to links.<href>, with lang <label> read only by screen readers. Only the copy keys listed may carry the mark. `fact`: the link must carry the transaction id written in that docs/FACTS.md row.

share._note: site/share.js: the phone share sheet when the browser has one, otherwise a panel with copy link and these targets. {url} and {text} are filled URL encoded by tools/site.py; the label of each target is lang share.targets.<id>.

og_build._note: tools/og.py (decision 0014). The vertical share image is composed from one committed 9:16 cue frame, scaled with lanczos; no new frame is generated. The title, the hook caption, the rower and the coin sit inside the centre 1.91:1 box (Facebook, Telegram), so also inside the centre 1:1 box (WhatsApp), which adds the domain and the fare figure. Text comes from the film: title from config/film.json, hook = caption id, figure = the 9:16 band with that fact.

banner._note: tools/banner.py (decision 0015). The banner note dates come from here. repo_check: auto = repository links are written hidden and site/repo.js shows them when repo_api lists the repository as public; on = always shown; off = never. deck: language code to a PDF path in this repository, empty = no deck link.

deck._note: tools/deck.py (decision 0016) prints site/deck/deck.html once per language with Chromium to `out` ({lang} filled), one 16:9 page per slide. Slide text is lang deck.*, ai.* and banner.* (the same sentences as the page); pictures are committed film frames. `stamp` holds, per language, the sha256 of the printed HTML and of the PDF, so a PDF printed from older text or replaced by hand fails the tests. `address_slide` is the slide that must show prize_address.
